BV.note: Norwegian government describes an uninhabited remote island. No public emergency telephone service was established by this collection; no mainland number is inferred.

HM.note: Australian Antarctic Program describes islands unoccupied by humans. No territorial emergency telephone service was established by this collection; no mainland number is inferred.

TF.note: Territorial administration describes districts without a permanent civilian population. Station or expedition contacts were not established as public emergency services; French mainland numbers are not assumed.

UM.note: The ISO code groups remote islands under different local arrangements. The refuge authority describes restricted access to many islands. No shared emergency number was established for the entire ISO territory; US911 is not assumed.

PN.note: Government guidance lists a police officer and locally raised VHF fire alarms, but no emergency telephone number.911 is unsupported.

GS.note: Government guidance directs visitors to their expedition leader or operator. No public emergency telephone number was established by this collection.

KP.note: Government guidance reviewed does not establish public countrywide emergency dialing numbers. Unreviewed local-only numbers from the secondary table are withheld. An empty object does not prove that no service exists.

SS.note: Current travel guidance states there are no central emergency numbers. ITU2023 reports112/777 police allocations, but operation and scope conflict with the current guidance; numbers are withheld pending reliable operational clarification.
